summary: One read-only command runs the independent profile, index-integrity, retrieval-quality, and optional adoption gates and returns either complete diagnostics or a bounded failed-only agent projection without fail-fast loss. An unavailable reader lock fails before gate execution; no lock, cache, snapshot or directory is created or repaired.

command.name: validate
command.syntax: shin-context --profile PROFILE --profile-dir PROFILE_DIR --root PROJECT --out-dir INDEX validate [--marker FILE] [--require-current] [--summary] [--strict]
command.exitPolicy: The command exits 0 only when every attempted gate reports ok=true and exits 1 after emitting all gate results when any attempted gate fails. CLI and configuration errors that prevent command startup retain shin.error.v1 behavior.

execution.processModel: Existing command implementations execute in-process and their single JSON stdout documents are captured into gate.result; no shell or child process is used.
execution.concurrencyBoundary: The CLI command boundary is single-threaded while aggregate capture is active. Internal gate workers do not write command documents to stdout.
execution.snapshotBoundary: Every generated-index gate targets the same explicit --out-dir. Each existing gate retains its own integrity and freshness semantics; validate does not create a new retrieval or ranking implementation.
execution.resourceBoundary: A bad allocation remains fatal rather than being converted into a partial validation result. Other gate-local typed failures are retained in gate.error and later independent gates still execute.
execution.generationPreparation: Within one validate invocation, check, read-only vacuum and exact eval/Pack freshness may share one independently generated expectation, capped at 256 MiB of retained generated bytes. Every gate still inspects actual outputs and runs all quality checks. Full effective profile, source inventory/content hashes and external link/Retool dependencies fence reuse. Changes, incomplete observations, unsupported dependencies or format differences disable sharing and retain independent generation. No persisted receipt or quality/publication certificate is created; standalone commands remain independent.

gates.skipRule: Recorded as skipped when --marker is omitted.

options.strict: Forwards strict policy to profile-check, doctor, vacuum, eval, pack-eval, and optional adoption-check. Strict eval and Pack eval already require exact current output.
options.requireCurrent: Requires exact current output in eval and Pack eval when strict mode is not selected. Check independently reports exact generated drift.
options.marker: Optional marker passed only to adoption-check. A safe absolute or dot-segment input below --root is normalized to one canonical repository-relative output path. Escape and symlink paths remain rejected. Marker omission is explicit skipped evidence, not a passing adoption claim.
options.summary: Selects shin.validation-summary.v2. Passed and skipped gates retain identity/status and elapsed timing. Eval and Pack eval use bounded failed-only projections; every failed gate retains bounded reason, summary, evidence, and remediation fields while complete diagnostics remain available from the named gate or full validate.

output.gateTiming: elapsed_ms is nonnegative steady-clock elapsed duration including gate execution and captured-result parsing, in both full and summary projections; null for a skipped gate. It is not CPU time or an authorization input.
output.preparation: Additive diagnostic object: generation_runs, reuses, invalidations, inventory_checks, verified_source_files/bytes, verification_ms, retained_bytes, fallback_reason. Verification counters describe completed explicit rehash passes, not all reads or physical disk I/O; time describes successful input-verification calls. No authority or outcome decision uses these numbers.

failureClasses.safety_findings: Non-info doctor issues whose stable id begins with unsafe- or secret-like-.
failureClasses.runtime_failures: Gate-local runtime, internal, resource, or filesystem errors captured before a normal command result was available.

output.diagnosticCompleteness: A failed gate never suppresses a later independent gate. Full projection retains every nested result. Summary projection keeps bounded whole-record failure evidence and safe diagnostic argv, omits successful nested payloads, and never claims to be the complete diagnostic tree.

summaryProjection.identity: Top-level profile, roots, normalized marker, execution policy, aggregate summary, exit status, and every gate identity/status are identical to full validation.
summaryProjection.truncationPolicy: The complete failed-gate result, including counters, diagnostic_budget, and detail_command, must fit gateDetailBudgetBytes. Whole evidence records are admitted by exact serialized-envelope measurement; no record is byte-sliced. When an eval or Pack failure exceeds the gate budget, a header preserves its identity, reasons and primary path. Pack headers carry passed=false. Counts expose eligible, returned, omitted, detail-omitted, and metadata-omitted diagnostics. Observer retains safe case identifiers, reasons and relative primary paths and reports truncation from either nested budget.

failureProjections.headerFallback: When one complete failure cannot fit, a bounded detail_level=header record preserves identity, reasons, and one verification path instead of silently dropping the failure.
failureProjections.suiteReasonBoundary: Freshness reasons are failures only when --strict or --require-current makes freshness part of ok.

summaryProjection.remediation: Every failed gate exposes a safe complete detail_command.argv with profile, profile-dir, root, out-dir, gate command, and applicable strict/current flags. Adoption-check uses its marker-owned route. Automatic execution and consumer/index mutation remain false.

boundaries: validate never runs build and never repairs an index
validate does not replace ASan/UBSan, Apple leaks, CTest, static analysis, performance, portable-install, release-contract, or ecosystem gates
validate does not weaken the project-owned permanent-adoption requirement for one canonical marker-derived output
validate contains no consumer vocabulary, paths, or product semantics
acceptance: a healthy non-strict fixture reports six passed gates and one skipped adoption gate
a strict profile warning fails configuration while both retrieval-quality gates still execute and pass
all zero-valued failure classes remain present for stable machine consumption
unknown and duplicate options fail with typed usage errors
summary output is smaller for a healthy validation and keeps failed-gate diagnostics below 64 KiB with explicit omission accounting
absolute and dot-segment marker inputs below --root normalize to the canonical relative marker while outside-root and symlink paths fail closed
the relocated portable binary runs validate successfully against its generated fixture index
